science.qualification: Photosphere color from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum, dimmed toward the limb by the quadratic law Claret & Bloemen (2011), A&A 529, A75 compute from ATLAS model atmospheres for the Johnson V band at 4,421.98 K and log g 4.68 (u1 0.755, u2 0.037): a model, because no fit of this star's limb is used. The disc is unresolved: no map or absolute brightness is implied. Self-luminous, so no lighting.

science.label: Campaign 4
science.description: Brightness of the star's surface that reproduces its light as it turns once in 25.2 days, fitted with starry to the K2 mission's own light curve of campaign 4 (its PDC-MAP flux) (the light varies by 0.21%; the map's curve leaves a scatter of 0.05%, the light's own noise being 0.03%). A light curve fixes how bright each longitude is, not the latitude of what darkens it. Reinhold & Hekker (2020, A&A 635, A43) list the star as a rotator in their table (VizieR J/A+A/635/A43/table2): a rotation period of 25.21 ± 3.86 d in campaign 4, with a periodogram peak of 0.3. The rotation and its period are theirs, taken as published; no criteria were applied to them here. No tilt of this star's axis is known: the map is made at 60°, the middle tilt of axes that point at random. Gaia DR3 lists 1 other star within 16 arcseconds, with 6.4% of their light and the star's together. A reduction made in this project, not a published map.
science.title: K2 · brightness map made here · Campaign 4

science.label: Color + brightness
science.description: The star's color (#ffbe93, its Color dataset) over the brightness map this project made from the star's light in K2 campaign 4 (February to April 2015): the map's scale, 99.5% to 100.5% of the mean surface, runs from a darker, richer tone of the same hue to the color itself. The contrast is drawn far stronger than it is, so the parts can be told apart: the darkest part gives 1% less light than the brightest. Longitudes are fixed by the light curve; latitudes and shapes are not. No color change of the spots is drawn: none is measured. A reduction made in this project, not a published map.
science.title: K2 · the star in its color over its brightness map · February to April 2015
